argument:
Solarvest's RM2.371bn backlog is a credible opportunity, but 89.1% EPCC exposure concentrates execution and cash-conversion risk. Revenue declined sequentially from RM270.5m to RM155.9m despite 13.2% year-on-year growth. The observed 12.2% net margin improvement does not establish that future project timing and margins will be stable.

Electricity-sales growth of 25.8% is constructive, yet it does not make the larger project book recurring cash. Debt and FCF remain unknown and the vendor trailing multiple is 48.00x. RSI above 82 with a five-bar pullback and below-average volume makes chasing especially difficult. A project-delay or cost-overrun downside is an execution scenario, not an observed new disruption.
key_points: Backlog is not cash; EPCC dominates exposure.
Sequential revenue contraction qualifies annual growth.
Funding evidence and near-term entry confirmation are incomplete.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull correctly identifies a growth runway, but its recurring-electricity argument does not neutralise 89.1% EPCC exposure. The sequential revenue decline demonstrates timing variability already present in the evidence; backlog size alone cannot establish profitable funded delivery.
